overview: Tajikistan is a landlocked country in Central Asia. Its capital and largest city is Dushanbe. Tajikistan became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991, and a civil war followed in the 1990s. Tajik, a language closely related to Persian, is the official language.

geography.text: More than 90 percent of Tajikistan is mountainous. The Pamir Mountains, sometimes called the 'Roof of the World', cover the east, and Fedchenko Glacier is one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions. Most people live in the lower valleys of the west and north.

history.text: Tajik cities such as Khujand stood on the Silk Road, and the region shared in Persian culture for centuries. It came under Russian control in the 1800s and became a Soviet republic. Tajikistan became independent in 1991 and then suffered a civil war from 1992 to 1997.

events.title: Alexander's city
events.text: Alexander the Great founds a city on the site of Khujand.

events.title: Russian rule
events.text: The region comes under Russian control.

events.title: Soviet republic
events.text: Tajikistan becomes a full Soviet republic.

events.title: Peace
events.text: A peace agreement ends the civil war.

government.text: Tajikistan is a presidential republic in which President Emomali Rahmon has held power since 1992. He has been given the title 'Leader of the Nation', and there is little room for opposition.

economy.text: Tajikistan is the poorest country in Central Asia. Money sent home by Tajiks working in Russia makes up around a third of the economy, one of the highest shares in the world. Aluminium, cotton and hydropower are other key industries.

culture.text: More than 90% of Tajikistan is mountainous, and the Pamir Mountains are called the 'roof of the world'. Tajik is a form of Persian. The Pamir Highway is one of the highest roads in the world.

items.title: Pamir Highway
items.text: A mountain road reaching over 4,600 metres.

items.title: Navruz
items.text: New Year at the spring equinox.

sport.text: Wrestling, judo and boxing are popular, and Tajikistan reached the Asian Cup quarter-finals at its first appearance in 2024. Gushtigiri, a traditional wrestling style, is national heritage.

items.text: Reached the Asian Cup quarter-finals at its first attempt.
